solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Chimney jack embosomed by familiar busty star: "tasty spread!"

indicators.note: to be embosomed is to be held to someone's bosom, so the first pieces sit inside the star's name

blocks.note: first part of PAM, the familiar short form of Pamela, as in Pamela Anderson
a lum is a Scottish and northern word for a chimney
J is the card abbreviation for jack
last letter of PAM, wrapped round the other pieces

explanation.surface: A tabloid caption about a busty celebrity hugging a chimney sweep, ending in a breathless food advert.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM and J go inside PAM to make PLUM JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Jam made from plums is a sweet preserve spread on bread or toast.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) Filthy rich old fart, so one is outed as would-be betrayer of Cameron

indicators.note: something filthy has been messed about and spoiled, so the remaining letters are jumbled
being outed means being put out, so that letter is removed from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written, as the anagram fodder
one is the Roman numeral I, the letter thrown out

explanation.surface: A Private Eye jibe at a wealthy old peer who turned on the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Ashcroft, a billionaire Tory donor, co-wrote a 2015 biography of David Cameron containing embarrassing allegations after being denied a senior post.
explanation.definitionFit: The donor fell out with the Conservative leader and published a damaging unauthorised biography, a kind of revenge betrayal.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Cabinet minister on edge causing uproar

blocks.note: Theresa May, then Home Secretary
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A senior politician on the brink of a breakdown sets off a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places one piece before the other in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder and chaos, the same state as a noisy public uproar.

clue.text: Baiter's position on Labour's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: an angle is a stance or point of view
last letter of Labour

explanation.surface: Someone who taunts others takes a stance on the Labour Party's future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baiter' reads as someone who taunts, but here it is someone putting bait on a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman using rod and line puts bait on the hook to lure fish.

clue.text: "Ineffective body with dodgy war ends around East" – as many an awkward question put to politicians

definitions.text: as many an awkward question put to politicians

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the jumbled letters sit around the next piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: the United Nations, often mocked as toothless
taken as written, as anagram fodder
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A sneer at the United Nations and its shady peace deals, followed by a dig at evasive politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The UN is often derided as a toothless talking shop, which is why it can be called an ineffective body.
explanation.definitionFit: Politicians famously dodge tricky questions, leaving them without a reply.

clue.text: Appearance unattractive, so poor prospects

definitions.note: a verb phrase defined by a noun phrase: things that look bad have poor prospects

blocks.note: looks means someone's appearance
bad as in unpleasant or unappealing

explanation.surface: An ugly face means a bleak future, the cynic's view of dating.
explanation.definitionFit: When a situation seems likely to end badly, people say the outlook is grim, or that things are unpromising.

clue.text: see 27dn.
Career: Boris's last to impress

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, the only one taken here

blocks.note: final letter of Boris
to impress is to stamp or print a mark

explanation.surface: A political career hinging on Boris Johnson's final attempt to win people over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun about jobs; here it is the verb meaning to rush along.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to dash headlong at great speed, just like running flat out over a short distance.

clue.text: Wet's resistance when protected by dame

indicators.note: something protected is shielded on all sides, so this piece sits inside the next

blocks.note: Dame Judi Dench, the actress
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A feeble politician's opposition, propped up only by a grand old lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' looks like the Thatcher-era insult for a soft Tory, but it is a verb. R goes inside DENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench something is to soak it thoroughly, making it very wet.

clue.text: Balls stuck in broadcasting device – quack appears?

indicators.note: a thing stuck in another is lodged inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: short for microphone
Ed Balls, the Labour politician

explanation.surface: A rude joke about something lodged in a microphone, with a duck noise heard on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was Labour's shadow chancellor; his surname makes the clue read as a smutty joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Quack is slang for any doctor, not only a fraudulent one, so it can stand for a medical practitioner.

clue.text: McDonnell, for one, packed onto boat!

blocks.note: hard as in tightly compacted
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A politician crammed aboard a ship like a refugee.
explanation.walkthrough: John McDonnell was Labour's left-wing shadow chancellor under Corbyn.
explanation.definitionFit: John McDonnell is an uncompromising socialist, an example of someone who sticks rigidly to strict party doctrine.

clue.text: Who delivers the news: "Monarch gets pissed on one"?

indicators.note: someone who gets drunk is all over the place, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
an means one

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about the sovereign getting drunk, or being urinated on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pissed on one' suggests an insult; 'pissed' is the anagram signal and 'on' places AN after.
explanation.definitionFit: The presenter who reads bulletins on a television news programme is called the anchor.

clue.text: Banking, having shafted mug, is making an indecent profit

indicators.note: to shaft is to drive a pole through, so the first piece is thrust into the middle of the second

blocks.note: start of CUP, a mug being a drinking cup
an aircraft banks by leaning into a turn
the rest of CUP, split by the inserted word

explanation.surface: A swipe at bankers who rip off gullible customers to make obscene profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' and 'mug' look like the City and its victims; LEANING goes inside CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is an idiom for making a large and easy fortune, often a shamelessly big one.

clue.text: A growing thing: getting Blair finally to admit suppressing article

indicators.note: finally points at the final letter of the name before it
to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so the word encloses the next piece

blocks.note: last letter of Blair
to own up is to admit
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Tony Blair is finally made to confess, while an awkward item is hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside OWN, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash is a tree, and trees are living plants that grow.

clue.text: Ill-informed Corbyn's ilk, looking very gloomy

blocks.note: Corbyn's kind are the political left
in the dark as in unlit and gloomy

explanation.surface: A jibe that Corbyn's followers are clueless and miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in the dark is an idiom for being denied information, so uninformed.

clue.text: see 27dn.
To be a real pain, Dave messed with dim Boris's heart

indicators.note: things that are messed with are disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
middle letter of Boris

explanation.surface: David Cameron tampering with the dim Boris Johnson's heart, a real nuisance to both.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave is David Cameron, Boris is Boris Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a severe annoyance to someone exasperates them until they feel they will lose their sanity.

clue.text: Admit leaving Brown with impossible seat (Bristol)

indicators.note: when something is leaving it departs, so it is taken out of the longer word
an impossible arrangement cannot stand, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written: Gordon Brown
to own is to admit, removed from the name
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An election-night line about Gordon Brown and an unwinnable constituency in Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristol' looks like part of the parliamentary seat; it is rhyming slang, as Bristol City rhymes with titty, so Bristols means breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang Bristol City stands for titty, so one Bristol is a female bosom.

clue.text: Brenda's slicing plonker's nuts

indicators.note: something slicing cuts into the middle of another, so it ends up inside it

blocks.note: start of BERK, British slang for an idiot, like plonker
Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, ER, plus the S of the possessive
the rest of BERK

explanation.surface: The Queen cutting off a fool's testicles, a lurid Private Eye fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: ERS goes inside BERK; a plonker and a berk are both British slang for a fool, and 'nuts' looks like the plonker's testicles but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Going wild with rage or frenzy is the same as being crazy, an informal sense of nuts.

clue.text: Nick to be a candidate? Cool!

blocks.note: to run for office is to stand as a candidate
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A cheerful reply to someone deciding to stand for election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name, perhaps Nick Clegg, but is the verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang: to run someone in is to arrest them, which is also what nick means in British English.

clue.text: Corbyn ultimately is obliged to produce sod all

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: last letter of Corbyn
ought expresses obligation

explanation.surface: A sneer that Corbyn is bound to achieve absolutely nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod all is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A nought is the figure zero, meaning nothing, which the slang phrase also means.

clue.text: "Duty to bow and scrape" carried out by some Swiss bank account holders?

definitions.text: carried out by some Swiss bank account holders?
definitions.note: a descriptive definition by example: the thing such people do

blocks.note: a duty is a tax on goods
a fiddler bows and scrapes the strings of the violin

explanation.surface: A sneer at fawning wealthy clients who hide their money in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow and scrape' looks like grovelling; the setter means playing a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret Swiss accounts are the classic way to evade paying what is owed to the revenue, a dishonest scam.

clue.text: Old ruler rejected shagging etc. with king

explanation.walkthrough: Xerxes was a king of ancient Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes the Great was a Persian emperor of the fifth century BC who invaded Greece.

clue.text: I declare Widdecombe a cat, right?

clue.text: Attitude and beliefs of those screwing around

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

clue.text: (& 8ac./17dn.) Working on Chinese nation to accept democratic leader? Resign!

blocks.clueFragment: Working on Chinese nation to accept democratic leader?
blocks.note: surface reading: an activist campaigning to make China accept a democratically chosen ruler

blocks.clueFragment: Working on Chinese nation to accept democratic leader?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the Han, the main Chinese people, take in the first letter of democratic, the start of the phrase, while someone working is told to quit

explanation.surface: A dissident labouring to bring democracy to China is told to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: HAN is the majority Chinese ethnic group and D is the leader of democratic, so the answer opens HAND; the rest is the idiom for leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Formally telling an employer you are leaving your job is the usual way of quitting a post.

clue.text: Sensitive reaction to pain, being thrust into Tracey's skirts

the cry when hurt
last letter of Tracey

explanation.walkthrough: OUCH goes between the outer letters of Tracey.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easily offended or irritable is described as thin-skinned, quick to take offence.

clue.text: Demanded by lawyer to keep Brenda?

blocks.note: to retain is to keep

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; her royal cipher is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is the advance fee a client pays to engage a barrister or solicitor's services.
